gauntlet.intent: T4 main-ladder baseline #3: SEEDED RANDOM INJECTS (deterministic/scripted, per tier spec -- the sim's event mechanism is fixed scripted events, not runtime Random.Shared/wall-clock, so 'seeded' here means fixed-tick-scheduled and reproducible across seeds 42/7/123, not stochastically timed) plus DYNAMIC EMCON CHANGE ON DETECTION. Two genuinely mechanical injects, both real engine-consumed fields (not narrative-only): (1) reinforcement_sub_inject_designated @ tick 10 -- pl-877-kilo-paltus-1992 is authored as a top-level `contacts` entry with appearAtTick=10 (ScenarioContactSimulator.Tick fires a real Unknown->Detected transition at that exact tick, confirmed at src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Sensors/ScenarioContactSimulator.cs:43), modeling a RED submarine reinforcement joining the fight mid-run; (2) sensor_degradation_inject_designated @ tick 14 -- a `jammers` entry with activeFromTick=14 (ScenarioJamResolver.ResolveJam gates on simTick < ActiveFromTick, confirmed at src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Sensors/ScenarioJamResolver.cs:22) degrades BLUE's f-16c-blk-52iq-falcon-2015 radar Pd against mig-29-fulcrum-c-1999 from that tick onward, modeling a RED EW/self-protection jamming inject. SCHEMA CONSTRAINT DISCLOSED for the EMCON dimension: ScenarioEmconResolver/CatalogRadarEmconResolver resolve EmconState once from the static emcon.units dictionary at scenario load (src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Scenario/ScenarioEmconResolver.cs) -- there is no engine-consumed field or event kind (MissionEventKind is only MissionTransition|EventFired, both pure OrderLog/fingerprint markers with no mechanical side effect) that mutates a unit's EmconState mid-run. This scenario expresses 'dynamic EMCON change on detection' honestly, not by inventing a new field: (a) f-219-sachsen-type-f124-2006 and ssn-774-virginia-blk-i-ii start radar Passive in emcon.units, modeling pre-detection emissions discipline; (b) the tick-10 reinforcement contact's Unknown->Detected transition is wired directly into the ONE real mission.triggers mechanic the engine actually runs on that transition (asw-reinforcement-detect-roe, escalating ssn-774-virginia-blk-i-ii/ka-27m-helix-a/s-185-u-35-type-212a from WeaponsTight to WeaponsFree) as the closest available, engine-consumed substitute for a detection-triggered posture change. This is the same disclosure pattern gauntlet-forge-20260727-1455-t4-c4 used for its single-ROE-flag domain-split gap -- a documented simulation-vs-schema limitation, not a hidden assumption.
gauntlet.oracle: Both EventFired codes (reinforcement_sub_inject_designated @10, sensor_degradation_inject_designated @14) must appear in the fingerprint regardless of engagement outcome. Before tick 10, BLUE's ASW group (ssn-774-virginia-blk-i-ii, ka-27m-helix-a, s-185-u-35-type-212a) stays WeaponsTight-denied on the c-s3-1 dipping-sonar contact on pla-885-severodvinsk-yasen; at/after tick 10 the pl-877-kilo-paltus-1992 reinforcement's Detected transition fires asw-reinforcement-detect-roe and the group may register ASW kills against either RED submarine for the remaining 14 ticks. BLUE's AAW/surface units (f-16c-blk-52iq-falcon-2015, f-310-fridtjof-nansen, nh90-tth-mrh90-taipan-2007) are never covered by a trigger in this scenario and are expected to stay WeaponsTight-denied for the full 24-tick run, contributing the denial floor. From tick 14 onward, f-16c-blk-52iq-falcon-2015's detection Pd against mig-29-fulcrum-c-1999 (c-s3-2) is expected to degrade per the activated jammer, illustrated as reduced/absent detection continuity rather than a fingerprint token (ScenarioJamResolver has no dedicated log entry of its own). RED (WeaponsFree) is expected to convert some of its own detections (c-s3-5, c-s3-6) into kills against BLUE.
